name: Notion
description: Pages, database rows and comments in a Notion workspace.

objects.label: pages
objects.description: Pages the integration has been shared with, including their text.

fields.label: content
fields.description: The page body as plain text.

fields.label: parent
fields.description: The page or database this page lives under.

objects.label: database rows
objects.description: Rows in a database. Filter by any property name.

fields.label: status
fields.description: Notion's built-in Status property; a database may have its own options.

fields.label: person
fields.description: A Person property such as Assignee or Owner.

objects.label: comments
objects.description: Comments on pages and database rows, including replies in a discussion.

actions.label: a database row
actions.description: One new row per record. Properties are matched to the database's columns by name.

actions.label: a page
actions.description: A new page under a parent page, either one per record or one for everything.

actions.label: a comment on each page
actions.description: Comment on the pages or rows in the source. Comments notify people who follow the page.

guidance: Notion is reached through the public API as an internal integration with a secret token; the integration sees nothing until a person shares each page or database with it from the page's Connections menu. Database properties are matched by name and type, so the plan should name the database and the properties it fills exactly as they appear. Prefer adding rows, pages and comments over editing existing page content, which the API can only replace block by block.

setup.notes: A workspace owner creates the internal integration at notion.so/my-integrations and then shares the pages or databases named in the plan with it.
